title: Nagaland: Wokha DFO Sivachar wins Eco Warrior Award
excerpt: Morung Express NewsDimapur | September 29Wokha Divisional Forest Officer (DFO) Suman Shivashankar Sivachar WM been honoured with the Eco Warrior Award 2026 for his contribution to environment conservation.Sivachar was among 15 forest officers recognised at the 4th Eco Warrior Awards and Eco Warrior Conclave held in New Delhi on September 29. The event was organised by the Indian Forest Service Association (IFSA) and Indian Masterminds.Under the Environment Conservation category, Sivachar was recognised for Amur falcon protection, community engagement and conservation of the Doyang Reservoir.Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Bhupender Yadav presented the awards and stressed that conservation is not merely a government responsibility but a national responsibility.Addressing the gathering, Yadav highlighted the growing challenges of climate change, extreme weather events, forest fires, water stress, habitat fragmentation and invasive species. He called for a landscape approach integrating forests, wildlife, agriculture, water, livelihoods and human settlements.The Minister also acknowledged the contribution of frontline forest personnel and tribal and forest-dependent communities in conservation.The Lifetime Achievement Award was presented to senior IFS officer Brij Kishore Singh, a 1976-batch officer of the Karnataka cadre, for his decades-long contribution to forest and wildlife conservation.Other awardees were recognised under categories including Protected Area Management, Wildlife Protection and Conservation, Community Connect, Best Use of Technology and Special Jury Award.The conclave also featured discussions on AI and technology for conservation and natural resource management, the role of corporates in forest management, and sustainable development and environmental ethics, informed a press release from the Ministry via PIB Delhi. title: Ep17: How Mira Kapoor Is Building India’s Luxury Wellness Brand | Building A $4 Mn Wellness Business
excerpt: In the latest episode of BT Podcast, Aabha Bakaya in conversation with Mira Kapoor, Founder, Dhun Wellness shares her journey from investor and brand builder to entrepreneur with Dhun Wellness. She shares why she identified a gap in India’s urban wellness market, how Dhun brings Ayurveda, recovery therapies, clinical longevity and preventive wellness under one roof, and why trust, safety and consistency are central to the business. Mira also opens up about Dhun Wellness’ expansion plans, including its 20,000 sq ft Delhi centre, the company’s recent $4 million fundraise from family offices and plans to enter Bengaluru and Hyderabad. She discusses key business metrics, including memberships and repeat visitors, her approach to investing in consumer brands, and her philosophy on finding businesses with long-term differentiation. She also talks about founder burnout, balancing entrepreneurship with family, and her vision of making Dhun Wellness India’s first luxury wellness brand.

title: IIT Bombay Suicide Case: Humanity narratives Vs Technological evidence
excerpt: With high-voltage developments in the aftermath of the death by suicide of second-year IIT-Bombay BTech student Sahil Wakode on September 18, inside the institute’s Powai campus, the case moved into a criminal investigation following allegations by his parents that he faced caste discrimination. The Mumbai Crime Branch is questioning students who were present in the examination hall where Sahil was reportedly caught for cheating and examining CCTV footage from the institute. His mobile phone has also been sent for forensic analysis. Sahil Wakode, a 22-year-old second-year student in the Department of Energy Science and Engineering from Yavatmal, Maharashtra, was found dead in his Hostel No. 4 room on the IIT-B Powai campus on September 18. The incident occurred hours after the examination. An FIR was registered under Section 108 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (abetment of suicide) and provisions of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act following a complaint by his father, Ravindra Wakode (also referred to as Chakradhar in some reports). The case was transferred to the Mumbai Crime Branch, led by an ACP-rank officer. However, with the reported surfacing of electronic evidences such as the CCTV footage of the examination hall where the alleged cheating using an AI application on the cell phone took place and the last phone call that Sahil reportedly had with a female friend has shed light on the stress that Sahil was under after returning to his room at the hostel. CNN-News18 has quoted highly placed Mumbai crime branch sources who have told them that the probe is focussing on a call made by IIT-B student Sahil at 2:30 PM. “Police told CNN-News18 that Wakode did not step out of his room post 1:30pm on Friday, adding that the investigation so far has revealed that he spoke to his girlfriend at 2:30 pm and admitted that he had made a “mistake.”,” says the report. “Mujhse galti ho gayi hai (I have committed a mistake)”, he reportedly said, adding, “My earlier thermodynamics paper didn’t go well, and now this has happened.” The report adds that according to investigators, Sahil’s friend asked him to stay calm, be patient and focus on his next papers. According to CNN-News18, there was no mention of any caste-related conversation during the phone call. They believe that this was the girlfriend’s last phone call with him. He stopped taking her calls thereafter. The investigation remains ongoing. No arrests have been reported as of the latest updates, and authorities continue to examine all available evidence, including CCTV recordings, digital material from the student’s phone, and statements from relevant individuals, before determining responsibility. The Crime Branch has maintained that the probe is at an early stage and that no final conclusions have been drawn. Mumbai Police sources indicate that the Crime Branch’s preliminary investigation into the death of IIT-Bombay (IIT-B) second-year BTech student Sahil Wakode has so far not found concrete evidence establishing Professor Suryanarayana Doolla’s role in abetment to suicide. Investigators have also not found eyewitness confirmation of any casteist remarks allegedly made against the student. The allegations of caste-based remarks, made by Sahil’s parents in their complaint, remain part of the ongoing investigation. According to police sources, some eyewitnesses stated that Professor Doolla was assigned examination-supervision duty on the day of the incident. During the mid-semester examination on September 18, 2026, Doolla allegedly noticed Sahil with a mobile phone and asked him to step outside the classroom. Sahil was then taken to the Head of Department, where another professor was also present, based on statements recorded by police. The Crime Branch has recorded the statements of Sahil’s father and mother. Professor Doolla, who invigilated the exam, along with two other professors have reportedly been questioned by the Crime Branch officials, but available reports as of September 23–24, 2026, indicate that either their formal statements have not yet been recorded or clear confirmation of completed questioning is yet to be circulated to the media by the police. CCTV footage from the examination hall and campus is being examined as investigators reconstruct the sequence of events. Officials have stressed that the probe is still at an early stage, no final conclusion has been reached, and all available evidence is under examination. What The CCTV Shows Fresh CCTV footage from an examination hall at IIT-B has surfaced, offering the first clear visuals of the moments before Sahil left the test on September 18. The recordings, captured between approximately 12:30 pm and 12:45 pm with about 15 minutes remaining in the mid-semester examination, show the student seated at a desk. He is seen bending slightly and looking toward his pocket. Professor Suryanarayana Doolla then approaches, speaks with him, and the student hands over a mobile phone before being taken aside from the other examinees. The Crime Branch is analysing CCTV feeds from the examination hall, campus grounds, and hostel premises to map Wakode’s movements. The footage provides a visual account of what transpired inside the examination hall and shows that between 12:30 pm and 12:45 pm, Professor Suryanarayana Doolla asked Sahil to leave the examination hall. Subsequent campus footage tracks the student’s movements after he exits the hall. Sahil was then seen outside the examination hall and, by around 1.25 pm, entering his hostel room, according to CCTV footage from the lobby. After that, the student did not leave his room, and later it came to light that he had died by suicide. No suicide note has been recovered so far. The visuals form a key part of the ongoing Crime Branch investigation into the student’s death. Police are examining feeds from the examination hall, campus pathways, and hostel areas to reconstruct the sequence of events. The phone recovered from the room has been sent for forensic analysis. Investigators are also examining the student’s mobile phone for digital evidence.
